transcript.text: What is the main goal you’d like this plan to support?
I want to run a mile as fast as I can, a time trial on the track in 6 weeks.
When you picture this plan working, what does it look like? For example: start with some easy jogging, then build up to longer runs.
Keep the easy mileage I have, add one short fast session a week, and finish with a proper time trial.

Your goal, in your words: "I want to run a mile as fast as I can, a time trial on the track in 6 weeks." Your recorded history covers 180 days. Your longest qualified continuous block is 63.0 minutes. In that time you've recorded 145 runs and 24 strength sessions. Your four-week jog average is 318.2 minutes per week. Your consistent running and strength work give you a solid base to start sharpening for a fast mile time trial. How would you describe where you are with your activity right now?
Yes, that's about right. I run most days.
Which days and times of day are realistically available for your runs?
Monday through Saturday mornings.
What kinds of exercise do you enjoy, and is there anything you’d rather avoid? For example: running and walking, but no gym.
I love running, and I do some strength work in the gym twice a week.
Is there anything we should plan around, like an injury or a health condition?
No issues.
It sounds like there's nothing we need to plan around — is that right? Say yes or tell me what I missed.
Yes, that's right.
How would you like me to communicate with you—plain, warm, or terse, and brief or full?
Plain and full, I like the detail.
Here's how the plan will run: we check in every Wednesday, and I plan 4 weeks at a time, building toward 2026-10-12. Does that work, or would you like to change anything?
Sunday check-ins and 4 weeks at a time is fine.
Here's how the plan will run: we check in every Sunday, and I plan 4 weeks at a time, building toward 2026-10-12. Does that work now, or anything else to change?
Yes, that works.
